litd2_period: Final years of the Last War through the Night of Sarn; post-Sarn institutions belong to epilogue and later history

eras.name: Dernière Guerre
eras.description: Several decades of continent-wide conflict sustained by dynasties, oligarchies, warlords and political manipulation.
eras.litd2_use: The full playable game takes place in its final years through successive historical runs.

eras.name: Batailles et opérations de la fin de guerre
eras.description: Each run is a battle, rescue, extraction, escort, infiltration, ceasefire operation or other event that contributes to the collapse of the war and the emergence of the three paths.

eras.name: Rupture de l'obéissance
eras.description: Soldiers, workers, cities and communities increasingly refuse to maintain the war. Sahra, Ilyan and Tala each become involved through different networks.

eras.name: Émergence des trois voies
eras.description: Corps, Esprit and Politique/Bien commun gradually become recognizable ideas through war experience, local assemblies, schools, rescue networks and the three founders' evolving doctrines.
eras.litd2_use: Narrative counterpart of in-run awakening choices and founder affinities.

eras.name: Nuit de Sarn
eras.description: A major attempt to end the war is sabotaged. Sahra, Ilyan, Tala, civilians and refusal networks converge. The three paths are explicitly understood together for the first time.
eras.litd2_use: Final playable run and narrative climax.

eras.name: Longues Assemblées
eras.relative_period: after Sarn and the collapse of the Last War
eras.description: Rotating assemblies across the continent transform the lessons and convergence of Sarn into durable political, educational and social institutions.
eras.litd2_use: Epilogue, postgame lore and bridge to the mature Concorde.

eras.name: Premier Pacte de Concorde
eras.description: A first group of cities accepts common limits on war and power while keeping local autonomy.
eras.litd2_use: Historical epilogue rather than the main playable ending.

eras.name: Première génération de transmission
eras.description: Mixed schools, early inter-city tournaments, civic mediation and common memorial places spread.

eras.name: Concorde mature
eras.description: Autonomous city-states cooperate through the Pact, shared institutions, protected routes, Grand Tournaments, Sanctuaries and the Three Awakenings education system.
eras.litd2_use: Future legacy shown in epilogue or historical codex.

litd2_run_structure.principle: A run is a historical operation inside the final years of the Last War, not a reset of time.
litd2_run_structure.world_progression: The war, routes, factions, refugees, refusal networks and founder doctrines evolve between runs.
litd2_run_structure.procedural_rule: Procedural generation may vary route, rooms, encounters and complications but never rewrite major historical facts.
litd2_run_structure.finale_rule: Sarn is the playable climax where the three paths converge explicitly; it is not their sole origin.
litd2_run_structure.post_sarn: Long Assemblies and the First Concord Pact occur after the playable finale and can be shown through epilogue/postgame content.

affinity_sources: refusal to equate strength with political legitimacy
responsible use of Light and perception

design_rules: Affinity represents trust, shared experience and mutual understanding rather than romance or morality.
Pure and hybrid builds are both valid affinity paths.
Repeated same-path farming has diminishing returns within a run.
Dual affinities unlock founder-pair scenes and composed-awakening context.
Balanced affinity unlocks additional convergence scenes but is not required to finish the game.
Affinity rewards are primarily horizontal: dialogue, events, lore, route variants and awakening variants rather than permanent stat inflation.
No affinity can permanently lock another path.

founding_principles: No war of conquest between signatory cities.
Martial victory grants no automatic political or territorial right.
Local autonomy remains protected under shared fundamental guarantees.
Collective punishment based on people, ethnicity or origin is forbidden.
Inter-city conflict must pass through mediation and arbitration before force.
Emergency powers must define their own expiration.
Political authority, justice and total military command cannot be concentrated in one person.
Major common decisions must leave a public record.
War responsibility is individual rather than hereditary or ethnic.
The Pact must remain publicly revisable by future generations.

social_development.citizenship: Belonging gradually shifts from bloodline and wartime allegiance toward residence, participation and protection under a city's institutions. Local models remain diverse.
social_development.war_displacement: Refugees are not systematically returned to supposedly natural ethnic territories. Mixed neighborhoods and families become part of the future cosmopolitan Concorde.
social_development.former_soldiers: Disarmament is paired with integration into road protection, rescue, reconstruction, civic guarding and martial schools rather than collective exclusion.
social_development.war_accountability: Responsibility is investigated individually. Collective vengeance against descendants, peoples or former enemy cities is rejected as a founding principle.
social_development.slavery_and_debt: The early Pact does not solve every economic abuse immediately, but the reconstruction period progressively rejects hereditary captivity and severe debt practices that reproduce wartime domination.
social_development.public_memory: Archives, witness lists and memorials record both victims and acts of refusal; memory is meant to preserve vigilance rather than inherited hatred.

education.Corps: At least one physical or martial discipline, with emphasis on effort, fear, restraint and limits.
education.Esprit: At least one artistic or perceptual practice; supernatural Light techniques remain optional rather than defining the Awakening.
education.Cite: History, argumentation, listening, propaganda recognition, institutions, mediation and real civic participation.
education.development_rule: At the end of LITD2 the three principles are clearly understood together, but the universal triple curriculum is built only across later generations.

institutional_evolution.early: temporary rotating wartime and reconstruction assemblies
institutional_evolution.mature: city Circles and Council of the Concorde
institutional_evolution.principle: no permanent capital owns the common institutions
conflict should be heard and documented before coercion

institutional_evolution.early: public reading of proposed clauses and objections
institutional_evolution.mature: formal civic review and Veilleurs du Pacte

institutional_evolution.early: mixed civilian protection groups and disobedient former soldiers
institutional_evolution.principle: security prioritizes protection, disarmament and de-escalation

institutional_evolution.early: emergency powers negotiated case by case
institutional_evolution.principle: exceptional authority must contain its own end

economy.start_of_litd2: Different city currencies, weights, debts and tolls reflect a fragmented wartime continent.
economy.reconstruction: Trade corridors reopen under shared protection; granaries and emergency stores are temporarily pooled during crises.
economy.gold_standard: Merchants and assemblies gradually use a common weight of gold for inter-city accounting while local coins persist.
economy.litd1_result: Centuries of normalization reduce the common monetary language simply to 'or'.
economy.core_tension: The Concorde regulates vital-resource hoarding without abolishing merchants, guilds, workshops or private exchange.

religion_and_culture.awakening_status: The Three Awakenings are not a religion.
religion_and_culture.religious_plurality: Older religions, ancestor traditions, animisms, philosophies and non-belief survive under common protections.
religion_and_culture.shared_culture: Common schools, routes, tournaments, festivals and civic practices create a continental culture without erasing local languages or customs.
religion_and_culture.aesthetic_rule: The mature civilization has a strong Asian visual and philosophical influence but is multiethnic and multi-people.

city_continuity.rule: A thousand years of reconstruction, migration and economic change separate these urban maps; do not assume a one-to-one city identity without explicit evidence.

rituals_and_shared_practices.name: Lecture des noms
rituals_and_shared_practices.mature_form: Public reading of selected names from many former camps during remembrance ceremonies
rituals_and_shared_practices.purpose: Remember victims without dividing them by former enemy identity

rituals_and_shared_practices.name: Salut sans bannière
rituals_and_shared_practices.origin: Meetings between disobedient soldiers from opposing armies
rituals_and_shared_practices.mature_form: Martial greeting used before some inter-city duels
rituals_and_shared_practices.purpose: Affirm that the fighter represents a discipline before a state or bloodline

rituals_and_shared_practices.name: Place vide
rituals_and_shared_practices.mature_form: Empty seat or open position in important deliberative spaces
rituals_and_shared_practices.purpose: Material reminder that opposition must remain possible

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Fragment du Premier Pacte
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: Very old clauses limiting conquest and emergency power.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: The Concorde began as a short revisable pact rather than a finished constitution.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Liste des sauvés de Sarn
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: Names from many peoples and former enemy cities written together.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: Sarn crystallized ideas and refusal networks built across years of war rather than receiving a supernatural revelation from nowhere.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Stèle des soldats sans bannière
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: Memorial honoring soldiers who stopped obeying orders during the Last War.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: The war ended through widespread refusal and civic action rather than one victorious army.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Monnaie de cité pré-Concorde
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: Local coin using a non-standard weight.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: The common concept of 'or' emerged from later inter-city standardization.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Tablette des trois noms
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: An early post-Sarn document lists Corps, Esprit and Bien commun rather than Corps, Esprit and La Cité.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: The third Awakening's vocabulary continued to evolve after LITD2.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: École des deux pratiques
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: A school teaches martial discipline and art but lacks a formal civic curriculum.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: The universal Three Awakenings education system took generations to become standard even after the three principles were recognized together.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Règles du duel sans conquête
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: Early tournament rules forbid territorial or political claims from victory.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: Grand Tournaments evolved from deliberate attempts to separate prestige from political domination.

litd1_trace_hooks.name: Plan des trois espaces
litd1_trace_hooks.surface: A simple memorial plan with a court, gallery and seatless circle.
litd1_trace_hooks.reveal: Sanctuaries began after Sarn as neutral places of shared memory, not religious temples.

canon_constraints: The Concorde is not a centralized empire.
The Three Founders are major synthesizers, not sole inventors.
The Night of Sarn is the final playable run and the crystallization of the Three Awakenings together, not their sole origin.
The playable runs are battles and operations from the final years of the Last War.
Founder affinities persist across runs and are fed by Corps, Esprit and Politique choices without becoming exclusive morality tracks.
Long Assemblies and the First Concord Pact continue after Sarn and belong to epilogue/postgame history.
The mature Concorde is not secretly decadent before the Fall.
The Fall remains caused by the external conspiracy and opening of the Gate in the Veil.
Every new LITD2 origin detail should have at least one possible trace or distortion in LITD1.
